techniques.name: Four live cells from frame 2
techniques.summary: There is no title. The film opens on a flush 2x2 grid where every cell is already mid-action (a line assembling, a counter ticking, an object orbiting, a pin dropping), so from its first frames the frame reads as one living system.
techniques.recipe: Root AbsoluteFill with a CSS grid (grid-template 1fr 1fr / 1fr 1fr, gap 0); every cell is overflow:hidden on the same stage colour (C.ink), so the seams disappear, with its content on the cell's own optical centre at 50-90% of the cell's width. Render each cell's scene at full 1920x1080 inside a wrapper with scale(0.5) and transformOrigin '0 0', so type keeps its native sizing and a cell can later go full-frame sharp. Wrap each cell's composition in Remotion <Loop durationInFrames={P}> with mutually awkward periods so the four never repeat in sync, and start each cell's first arrival by frame 2-6 on its own E.out curve with no shared global ease: for example a line converging with SPR.word, a Roll counter driven by countSteps(..., E.out), and an orbit whose angular speed decays as w = 11.25*e^(-t/10) + 2 deg/f, with satellites spawning on f10, f18 and f28. Only the one story element in each cell (pin, payoff word, button) gets C.accent; everything else stays greyscale. Merge every cell's cut frames into one list and nudge apart any two that fall within 6 f, and use no per-event SFX: one continuous groove carries the sound.
techniques.timing: First arrivals on f2, f2, f2 and f6 (no cell later than f8). Typical entrances: a type lockup settles in 18 f on E.out, a counter finishes in 28 f. Loop periods 260 / 462 / 244 / 428 f. Something changes somewhere about every 20 f (longest gap about 62 f). Cells 960x540 at 1080p.
techniques.use_when: A hero or social loop that must show several features at once, or a launch whose first second has to prove breadth.
techniques.avoid_when: The story needs one idea at a time, a single-message sting, or a 9:16 frame where the cells would shrink below about 540 px wide.

techniques.name: Macro number scramble, one-frame snap-out
techniques.summary: Huge digits fill and overflow the frame, re-rolling every frame. On one frame the view cuts back to the whole figure, which rolls into the final metric and holds: the number is the hook before any brand appears.
techniques.recipe: Lay out the final figure once with typeStyle('display') (tabular figures, fixed group separator) at a size where the whole string spans about 0.9 W, and draw each digit column as a Roll-style strip whose mask stays 1.6 lines tall during the macro phase, so outgoing digits stack and overflow vertically. Macro phase: scale the wrapper to 1.22 about the frame centre and, on every whole frame (fd), give 1-2 columns a new digit from rand(`${seed}:${fd(frame)}`). Snap: on a single frame decided with fd (so the motion-blur sub-samples agree), cut the scale to 1.0 with no tween, clip the masks to one line and lock the columns left to right 3 f apart until the final string is forced; then hold on breath (scale +0.065%/f) with no glints or sparkles, and keep the brand out until the end lockup. Sound: five dry glitch ticks inside the first 0.6 s, then the bed drops at least 30 dB within one frame on the lock frame and stays silent through the hold; reuse the identical tick cluster under the closing sting as a bookend.
techniques.timing: Macro 29 f; snap 1 f at f29; settle 12 f; final string forced from f41 (0.68 s); hold 72 f with only the scale drift. Ticks at about 0.17, 0.23, 0.31, 0.36 and 0.40 s.
techniques.use_when: The strongest proof is one metric (users, hours saved, uptime) and the film earns attention with the outcome before the brand.
techniques.avoid_when: There is no credible or impressive number, or the tone is calm and premium.

techniques.name: Mark builds, then is thrown into a macro of itself
techniques.summary: On frame 1 a dot swells into the brand mark. The mark grows briefly, holds for a breath, then shrinks away faster and faster and hard-cuts at peak speed to a frame-filling macro of the same mark, which keeps pulling back.
techniques.recipe: Show the mark only; the wordmark lockup is kept for the end. A 12 px dot at frame centre scales into the 320 px mark over 18 f on E.out, while a wrapper grows 0.83 -> 1 on E.out over 32 f from f8; then hold 8 f. Exit: wrapper scale 1 -> 0.55 over 20 f on E.in, with the hard cut on the exit's last (fastest) frame. The next shot opens on the same mark at the same screen point, its k multiplied by zoomHandoff(t, v0, 24) with v0 = zoomSpeed(kOut, cut - 1) (about -0.168): it starts near 2.2x and slows to 1x with no speed step at the cut, revealing the stage and the first UI as it settles. No overshoot anywhere; the master's motion-blur pass handles the fast frames (incoming edges peak at about 59 px/f).
techniques.timing: Dot to mark 18 f on E.out (edge about 49 px/f on its first frame); grow 32 f from f8; hold 8 f (f40-48); exit 20 f on E.in (f48-68), cut at f68 (1.13 s); macro pull-back 24 f through zoomHandoff from about 2.2x.
techniques.use_when: A brand-first logo sting where recognition must land in under half a second and the energy must pour into the next shot.
techniques.avoid_when: The mark is unfamiliar and needs a longer hold to be learned, or the film already uses a scale-continuity cut elsewhere. Never use it to show the full lockup.

techniques.name: Sparse intro, drop on the first hard cut
techniques.summary: (Sound and picture.) The first ~2 s carry only light plucks or a filtered, wide pad under the opening type; the low end and the kick land exactly on the frame where the punchline card or first product shot cuts in.
techniques.recipe: Arrange or edit the track so bar 1 has no sub and no kick and sits about 14 dB under the body, sounding at intent from frame 0 with no fade-in across the first bar: a steady filtered bed of plucks or pad, which may step up a few dB at the half-bar. Keep it wide (side about 3 dB under mid) and narrow it on the drop (side 16-19 dB under mid). Put the first hard cut on a downbeat, for example b(2) in src/timeline.ts (frame 120 at 120 BPM). Schedule the kick on that exact frame in src/sync.ts and the first sub swell 8-12 f before it. Keep the intro picture to one line or two short cards (2 words each at most) so reading fits the space; per-word ticks ride on top at a constant level.
techniques.timing: Intro 117-156 f (1.95-2.6 s); about +14 dB from intro to body; sub 8-12 f before the cut; kick on the cut frame (within 1 f).
techniques.use_when: Almost any film that opens on type and then shows the product with a tension-and-release shape.
techniques.avoid_when: Stings under 4 s, openers designed to be loud from frame 0 (live grid, macro scramble), or a drop that cannot land on a whole-frame cut.

techniques.name: Cursor into a field, two-stage push, typed provocation
techniques.summary: A small search pill sits still on a dark stage; a text cursor drifts in, the camera pushes in twice to a macro framing, and a provocative query types into the field before any brand appears.
techniques.recipe: Lay out the pill as world content under the anchor camera (camera(lc(A, B, t)) from src/lib/camera.ts), anchored on the caret. An I-beam SVG, placed by transform only as Cursor is, is already travelling on frame 0: it arrives on cursorArc (bow 0.2) over 30 f on E.glide, with a soft offset shadow (a copy blurred 6 px at 35% black, offset about a quarter of its height). The camera holds for the first 24 f, then push 1 takes k from 1 to 2.16 over 42 f on E.cam and push 2 from 2.16 to 7.2 over 44 f on E.glide (lc mixes k in log space, so the zoom rate stays even). Start TypeOn (cps 30) at about 60% of push 2 and feed typeOn's followX into the camera anchor through a 6-10 f lag so the camera tracks the caret without stepping; size the pill so one character advances at most 40 px on screen at 7.2x, which keeps the caret-following scroll of the typed text under 20 px/f. Draw no halo around the pill. Sound: micro ticks only (2-6 ms bursts high-passed above 4 kHz, at most one per word, 18-24 dB under the bed, with 20% seeded jitter in timing and gain), muted once the drums enter.
techniques.timing: Camera still for 24 f while the cursor flies in from frame 0 (30 f on E.glide); push 1 42 f (f24-66, peak 0.077 ln k per frame); push 2 44 f (f66-110, peak 0.082 ln k per frame); 7.2x in total over 88 f; typing from about f92 at 30 characters/s, each character at most 40 px wide on screen.
techniques.use_when: AI, search or command products, or any opener whose hook is a question the product answers.
techniques.avoid_when: The product has no input field, the film's camera grammar is flat, or the query runs past about 40 characters (the macro framing cannot hold it).
techniques.correction_note: Source calls the 24-66 and 66-110 segments 88 f. Their combined span is 110 - 24 = 86 f.

techniques.name: Oversize line flies through, restarts small
techniques.summary: A huge fragment of the headline, about a quarter of frame height, brakes in from the right with its letters fading on as it slows, then dissolves; three frames later the same line restarts small and centred so it can be read.
techniques.recipe: Start the big line's clock 6 f before the film's first frame (t = f + 6), so frame 0 already shows its first letters fading on as it brakes. Layer 1: the line at about 270 px, weight 500, colour rgba(255,255,255,0.65) on C.ink (or over a single-hue wash), with x = startX + inertia(t, 0, -70, 0.89).x (601 px of travel from 70 px/f). Per-character opacity is 0.65 * prog(t, 6 + 1.5i, 12 + 1.5i, E.smooth), so letters only resolve once the speed drops below about 20 px/f, and the whole layer fades 1 -> 0 over its last 7 f on E.smooth while it is still sliding. Start layer 2 on the next frame, with no empty frames between: a dissolve to an empty frame and a fresh start reads as the film restarting. Layer 2: the same line at reading size with its final centred layout precomputed, per-character opacity prog(t, 1.3i, 1.3i + 5, E.smooth), and container x = inertia(t, 0, -10.8, 0.88).x: an 84 px drift that lands exactly centred and never passes 12 px/f. Keep the opening type translucent and make the end card solid white, so the film reads as a question becoming an answer.
techniques.timing: Big line visible from f0 (its clock t = f + 6) to f35: slide 39 f, about 35 px/f at t = 6 and 17 px/f at t = 12; letters 6 f each, 1.5 f stagger; fade over the last 7 f. No gap; small line from f36, 13 characters in 17 f, drift settled in about 40 f.
techniques.use_when: The headline has a thesis word worth previewing big, in a dark, energetic launch.
techniques.avoid_when: Light stages where 65% white loses contrast, or headlines longer than about 5 words whose big fragment will not read. Also avoid it when the big fragment would sit still and cropped at both edges at any point: viewers read an oversized, cropped line that vanishes and then restarts small as a false start, not a preview. It has to travel every frame it is on screen.

techniques.name: Problem pile-up, freeze, turn
techniques.summary: The film opens inside the problem: cards, alerts or rows pile in faster and faster while a counter climbs, the picture freezes for a breath of true silence, and the turn hits on the downbeat.
techniques.recipe: Frame 0 already holds 2-3 overlapping cards. Arrival k comes gap_k = max(4, 14 * 0.88^k) frames after the previous one, so the pile accelerates, and each card rises from +40 px on SPR.firm with opacity over 8 f on E.smooth and a slight rotation of rand(k) * 6 - 3 deg. A corner counter climbs with Roll and countSteps(..., E.in) while the camera's k is multiplied by breath(prog(f, 0, end, E.in), 0.04). At peak density comes a designed freeze of at most 15 f, with the picture held and the bed and every tail cut dead; then the turn lands on the next downbeat b(...): the pile implodes on E.in, or the frame cuts to the answer. Sound: one soft tick per card, each 1 dB louder than the last, ending in the silence.
techniques.timing: 14 arrivals in about 100 f (gaps 14, 12, 11, 9.5, 8.4 ... down to 4 f); freeze of 15 f at most; turn on the next downbeat.
techniques.use_when: Problem-first launches whose pain is volume: notifications, tickets, tabs, invoices.
techniques.avoid_when: The pain is not about quantity, the brand film is calm, or the film already uses its one freeze elsewhere.

techniques.name: Finished result first, then rewind
techniques.summary: The film opens on the finished end state at its most impressive, holds for a beat, then visibly rewinds every element back to the empty start, where the story begins playing forward.
techniques.recipe: Every element is a function of frame, so remap time once at the act root: local = f < r0 ? T_end : T_end - (T_end - T_0) * prog(f, r0, r0 + R, E.smooth), with R = 36-48 f. Pass local to every component and decide discrete state with fd(local); entrances then replay backwards, and E.out arrivals become accelerating exits. Open at T_end with breath (+2.5%) over a 40 f hold. The rewind's peak rate is 2.86 × (T_end − T_0) / R times real time, so rewind at most about 120 f of build (about 8x at the peak for R = 42); for a longer build, set T_0 to a later, partly built state. Any element whose reversed move would pass 60 px/f, and any readable text that would pass 20 px/f, fades out over the rewind instead of travelling. Put one short filtered reverse swish under the rewind and a click on its last frame, then play the walkthrough forward from T_0 on the next beat.
techniques.timing: Hold 40 f; rewind 36-48 f on E.smooth (peak about 8x real time, at most about 120 f of build); forward play from the next beat.
techniques.use_when: Walkthroughs and feature films whose output is visually rich and readable at a glance.
techniques.avoid_when: An end state that needs explaining, or more than about 30 state changes (the rewind turns to mush).

techniques.name: A click starts the film
techniques.summary: From frame 0 a cursor is already travelling toward the one button on an otherwise bare stage; it presses, and the button floods open into the first scene.
techniques.recipe: C.paper stage with a single button (the product's primary action) slightly below centre. Cursor follows cursorArc(a, b, prog(f, -6, 18, E.glide), 0.2), so frame 0 is already mid-path because the clock starts 6 f before the shot. pressAt(f, 22) drives the cursor's press, and the button dips by 1 - 0.03 * hitPulse(f - 22, 2, 5). Iris starts at the press frame minus 1 (24 f, E.out in log space) from the button's centre and reveals the first scene inside it. Put the click SFX 0-1 f before the press frame, with nothing before it.
techniques.timing: Cursor arrives f18; press f22 (4 f down, 8 f recoil); iris f21-45; first scene live from f45.
techniques.use_when: UI walkthroughs and feature films where a single action is the product ('one click to ...').
techniques.avoid_when: Products that act on their own, or films where the cursor never returns after the hook (it breaks continuity).

techniques.name: Cut in mid-sentence, pull back to the line
techniques.summary: The film opens inside one giant word, its first letter cropped by the frame edge as if cutting into a thought mid-sentence; after a beat the camera pulls back to reveal the whole sentence at reading size.
techniques.recipe: Lay out the whole sentence once at display size (TYPE.display, 120 px) as world content and frame shot A at k = 3.2 on the key word, offset so its first glyph is about 40% cropped by the left edge. Frame 0 is already settling: a vertical inertia(f, 0, 3, 0.8) of about 13 px, then a 0.3 px/f drift through a 36 f hold. Pull back with lc(A, B, prog(f, 36, 92, E.dolly)) to k = 1 with the sentence centred; the log-space zoom keeps the rate even, and glyphs 600 px from the anchor stay under about 20 px/f. The neighbouring words exist from the start with no fades and simply enter the frame as it widens.
techniques.timing: Settle 12 f; hold 36 f; pull-back 56 f from 3.2x to 1x on E.dolly (peak about 0.032 ln k per frame).
techniques.use_when: Copy-led launches built on one charged word, in calm-to-medium films.
techniques.avoid_when: The key word is short or ordinary (the crop will not intrigue), or the film already opens on another zoom-out (icon card, macro number).

source_note: cinetic source recipes. Evidence counts are unverified source claims; evidence 0 has no corroborating count. Starter paths/helpers belong to the source project; read techniques.json before translating. Production reads follow video-brief/COPY.md.
